outcomes.statement: Apply safety standards to prevent injuries in the agricultural equipment technician workspace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2B: Personal Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss worker and employee rights and responsibilities as they relate to workplace safety and how they can prevent injuries.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common safety hazard categories and hierarchy of control common to the agriculture equipment service industry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess and mitigate the risks (e.g., slips, trips, falls, burns) and potential safety hazards (e.g., exposure to chemicals, gasoline, diesel) in the agricultural technician workspace.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the benefits of completing the different certifications and programs offered by Work Safe Sask, Sask Safety Council, Motor Safety Association, Agricultural Health and Safety Network, Sask Prevention and the Ministry of Labour Relations and Workplace Safety.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and explore basic safety procedures (e.g., storage and maintenance of tools, clean workspace and caution when working at high heights and around large equipment) as they apply to an agricultural equipment technician.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a list of rules for workplace safety including proper personal protective equipment (PPE), sanitation, neat and tidy work area and reporting workplace accidents and safety incidents.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the dangers of working in a confined space (e.g., sprayer tank, combine grain tank and barn manure tank or pit).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate the utilization and maintenance of protective devices on equipment.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform proper lockout and de-energizing of equipment before beginning inspections or repairs.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify the advantages and disadvantages of using each category of industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE) for respiratory, hearing, sight and body protection such as masks, ear plugs or earmuff, safety goggles and shields, gloves, footwear and aprons.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate PPE cleaning procedures.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe hazards from the misuse of oxy-acetylene welding equipment (e.g., tanks, hoses and gauges) and take measures to avoid unintentional injuries caused by flashback and backfire.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Locate and demonstrate the correct use of safety equipment (e.g., eye wash station, shower, first aid station, shop ventilation, fire extinguishers and caging devices) in the workplace.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Post and maintain emergency phone numbers in a visible location.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Discuss appropriate actions in the event of an injury in the workplace, including whom to contact, how to report and first-aid procedures.

outcomes.statement: Investigate proper handling of hazardous materials to prevent injury in the workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2D: Hazardous Materials (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the importance of and methods used to maintain a clean workplace.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify hazardous materials and relevant Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) procedures to manage them in the workspace.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) regulations for the storage of hazardous wastes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe and utilize the four parts of WHMIS 2015 (i.e., hazard identification and product classification, labels with warning symbols, safety data sheets (SDS), worker education and worksite specific training) to handle hazardous materials safely.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the correct environmental handling, cleanup and waste disposal of lubricants (e.g., oil and grease), coolants, fuel, filters, cleaners, containers and tires in accordance with local bylaws and provincial guidelines.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify control measures according to the hierarchy of controls, to prevent exposure to hazardous wastes and toxic chemicals.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the methods used to remove and dispose of chemical residue (e.g., fertilizer and pesticide spray) from application equipment.

outcomes.statement: Examine proper handling of equipment to ensure biosecurity and food safety.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2F: Biosecurity and Food Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the importance of ensuring biosecurity in agricultural industries.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Outline the management practices that should be put in place when working with agricultural equipment to ensure biosecurity.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the correct environmental handling, cleanup and disposal of waste products found in agricultural equipment being serviced.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize how the Safe Foods for Canadians regulations and Canada Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) program may affect a repair technician’s process in servicing agricultural equipment.

outcomes.statement: Investigate processes in the pre-delivery inspection and transportation of agricultural equipment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7B: Pre-delivery Inspection and Transportation of Agricultural Equipment (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 7A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the role of the Ministry of Highways, Infrastructure Permit system and the Traffic Safety Act in the transportation of farm equipment on provincial highways and roads.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of a pre-delivery inspection (PDI) for specific agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the adjustments (e.g., calibrations, clearance, function tests, hydraulic and electrical connections and speed adjustments) made to specific agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Perform adjustments to chosen agricultural equipment following the manufacturer’s safety procedures.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the purpose and methods to ballast a tractor according to the operator’s manual.

outcomes.statement: Locate agricultural equipment service information utilizing appropriate tools and sources.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Agricultural Equipment Service Information and Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Summarize the type of information available from common agricultural equipment service information sources (e.g., apps, computers, diagnostic charts, manuals, scan tools and technical bulletins).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of proper communication with parts personnel.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the use of parts codes and acronyms used in an electronic service tool (EST).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine correct service information such as torque specifications, wiring diagrams and disassembly/assembly procedures from appropriate sources.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate care in handling computers, manuals and scan tools.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze vehicle identification numbers (VIN) and engine emission compliance labels.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the strategies (e.g., contacting the manufacturer engineers and online forums) used by technicians to gather information that is not readily available from service material.

outcomes.statement: Investigate common agricultural equipment diagnosis and repair processes.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Agricultural Equipment Diagnosis and Repair Processes (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow manufacturer and industry safe work practices when diagnosing and repairing agricultural equipment, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common steps (e.g., identify, diagnose, repair and confirm the repair) of agricultural equipment repair processes.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe common practices and procedures (e.g., diagnosing, torquing, measuring, lifting and cutting) involved in agricultural equipment repair.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use service information to identify proper processes for repairing a specific problem.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the importance of accurate service records for the dealership business processes.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the components of single and multi-segment work orders for different types of repairs.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Follow the path of a work order and its connections to various roles and departments in an agricultural equipment dealership.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Complete a work order for different scenarios indicating the complaint, cause and corrections required.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify and document required components, create a parts list and cost estimate for a specific repair or modification.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Describe repair processes for identified issues or modifications.

outcomes.statement: Explore the function and operation of electrical circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14A: Fundamentals of Agricultural Equipment Electrical Systems (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Follow safe work practices (e.g., avoid sharp material and hot parts or tools) when working with electrical circuits, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe major electrical concepts including basic atomic structure and conductor, insulator and semi-conductor materials.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Define current, resistance and voltage and state their units of measurement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the factors (e.g., wiring, connection quality and corrosion) that affect resistance and their effect on current and voltage.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Differentiate between AC and DC circuits and identify where they are used in electrical circuits in agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Distinguish between the characteristics of series, parallel and series-parallel electrical circuits.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify different types of switches and their purpose.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of a controller area network binary unit system (CANBUS).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Classify common types of electric motors.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Diagnose, repair and confirm the repair of electrical circuits by soldering, splicing and taping wires and connections.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Assess the quality of and adjust electrical repairs.

outcomes.statement: Examine agricultural equipment electrical systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14B: Advanced Agricultural Equipment Electrical Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., ground static electricity, avoid the presence of water and disconnect the batteries) when working with agricultural equipment electrical systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the use of electrical and electronic components (e.g., sensors, actuators and switches) in agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Perform mechanical adjustments (e.g., camera, headlight and sensor alignments) to agricultural equipment electrical system components according to manufacturer’s specifications.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe wiring terminology and principles of electrical wiring.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and select appropriate wire gauge, connectors and circuit protection devices like fuses when working on electrical systems.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine electrical system schematic diagrams and service manuals to help diagnose electrical problems.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Perform common electrical tests (e.g., current, parasitic draw, resistance, voltage and voltage drop) using electrical testing equipment like a multimeter.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Provide examples of common faults (e.g., open circuit, short circuit and burned-out fuse or bulb) that may occur in agricultural equipment electrical circuits.

outcomes.statement: Investigate agricultural equipment computer systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Agricultural Equipment Computer Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices in dangerous situations (e.g., hot components, pinch points, shock hazards and static electricity discharge) when working with agricultural equipment computer systems and their components, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the operation of computer-controlled fuel systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Retrieve fault codes from the memory of an agricultural equipment computer system using an electronic service tool (EST) or onboard diagnostic system.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the diagnosis and repair of agricultural equipment computer systems following the appropriate fault code diagnostics.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore how to download software updates on agricultural equipment computer systems.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the diagnosis, service and repair of engine fuel delivery systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 20: Fuel Delivery Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., handle and store fuel safely, and be aware of pressurized fuel and fire hazards) when working with fuel delivery systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the operation of fuel delivery systems (e.g., high pressure commonrail, lift-pump, mechanical and unit injectors).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify different fuel types and additives (e.g., anti-gel and lubricant) used in agricultural engines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the benefits of using fuel additives.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment (e.g., fuel pressure gauge) to test fuel delivery systems.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform fuel delivery system scheduled maintenance (e.g., fuel filter change and system flush).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose, repair, and confirm the repair of common fuel delivery system faults (e.g., faulty filters, clogged injectors, leaks and lift-pump replacement).

outcomes.statement: Explore agricultural equipment intake, exhaust and emission systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21: Intake, Exhaust and Emission Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of hot surfaces and use of pipe bending equipment) when working with intake and exhaust systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the components and structure of agriculture equipment intake systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of the air intake system to the performance of the engine.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Summarize the regulations governing emission control of diesel engines.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify exhaust system components such as exhaust gas recirculation (EGR), selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system and diesel particulate filter (DPF).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of the components such as diesel nitrogen oxide (NOx) sensors, DPF, mixing chambers and diesel engine fluid (DEF) injectors of the emission control system in diesel engines.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the common issues (e.g., putting DEF into the diesel tank, contamination and improper storage) related to the use of DEF.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain how to regenerate a DPF.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Inspect and evaluate exhaust systems for blockage, corrosion, leaks, mounting issues and noise.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify the hazards associated with operating engine exhaust systems, including carbon monoxide in enclosed spaces and excessive noise levels.

outcomes.statement: Examine the component parts and operation of agricultural equipment hydraulic systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24: Agricultural Equipment Hydraulic Systems (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., avoid contact with pressurized hydraulic fluids and brake fluids contacting painted surfaces) when working with hydraulic systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the difference between pneumatic and hydraulic systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the uses of pneumatic systems.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the properties of different hydraulic fluids (e.g., brake, power steering, transmission and lifting systems) including the three main varieties (e.g., petroleum, mineral and synthetic).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain why one hydraulic fluid cannot be used for all applications including why an application-specific additive package may be required by a manufacturer.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper disposal of used hydraulic fluids.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Summarize potential environmental concerns of hydraulic fluids.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the parts (e.g., reservoir, pump, valves and actuator) of a hydraulic system.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the different types of fittings including thread style, function and uses.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain how Pascal’s law applies to hydraulic systems.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Investigate common hydraulic system component failures (e.g., filter, hose and pump) recognizing to never use a part of the body to detect a hydraulic leak. (e.g., never use your hand to run along a pressurized line).

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Identify the advantages of a hydrostatic drive.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Explain how a hydrostatic drive works.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the diagnosis, service and repair of agricultural equipment heating and ventilation systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27: Heating and Ventilation Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 26

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., check coolant pressure and temperature and watch for pressurized refrigerants and moving components) when working with agricultural equipment heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper disposal of used coolants.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the potential environmental concerns of coolant disposal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify how the cooling and heating systems are connected.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform common HVAC system tests (e.g., visual inspection, coolant and pressure tests and leak detection) and maintenance procedures (e.g., flushing the heater core and checking fluid levels).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the importance of following the manufacturer’s recommendations for cleaning, maintenance and replacement of cab ventilation filters.

outcomes.statement: Examine irrigation systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 28: Irrigation Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history and development of agricultural irrigation systems.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of using irrigation systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the common types (e.g., surface, sprinkler, drip and subsurface) of irrigation systems.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the components of typical irrigation systems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the fundamental operation of the different types of irrigation systems.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify possible problems that can develop with irrigation systems and the processes required to repair them.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the use of technology in agricultural equipment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 29: Emerging Agricultural Technology (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate how a need in agriculture drives the development of new technologies.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the current uses of technology (e.g., GPS, sensors and self-driving) in agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research and describe the use of emerging technologies designed to improve agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the environmental impact of emerging technologies.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze the benefits, disadvantages and cost of self-driving, autonomous and robotic vehicles in agricultural operations.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the development and use of new fuels to power agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the benefits of using telematics and hyper precision to monitor and regulate movement (e.g., turn compensation) of agricultural equipment.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine technology such as electric drives and header height control.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate the development of automation to increase the production and efficiency of specialized agricultural industries.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research a recent development in agricultural equipment technology.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe tasks that would benefit from technological advancement.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Predict future trends in technologies used in agricultural equipment.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80B: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Participate in a work placement experience.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 81B: Work Study Placement (Optional) · Suggested Time: 25-50 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 80B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply relevant skills and abilities during the work placement experience.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Document knowledge and awareness of employment standards, safety, workplace ethics, rights and responsibilities, occupational health and safety, and networking observed during the work placement.

outcomes.statement: Relate a work placement experience to personal and career goals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 82B: Work Study Follow-up (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 81B

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Reflect on the attainment of personal and learning goals.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Update personal career documentation (e.g., resume, portfolio) following the work placement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In appreciation prepare a letter, note, card or other communication for the work placement employer.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop and/or revise personal and career goals based on the work placement experience.

outcomes.statement: Investigate business opportunities in the agricultural equipment industry.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 85B: Agricultural Equipment Technician Business Opportunities (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the types (e.g., dealerships and specialty shops) of business opportunities available in the agricultural equipment industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore agricultural equipment-related business opportunities in sectors such as automotive, leisure or heavy machinery.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore business opportunities in servicing agricultural equipment in specialty (e.g., apiculture, berry farms, sod farms and dairy farms) agriculture operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the advantages and disadvantages of different business ownership models, including sole proprietorship, partnerships and private corporations.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the role of franchises as a business ownership model in the agricultural equipment industry.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research the requirements (e.g., registering business name, collecting and remitting taxes, registering with WCB, licensing and zoning) for establishing a business in one’s community.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research the importance of sustainable business practices such as providing quality customer service, following environmental guidelines and employing qualified and certified personnel.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the advantages of and requirements for obtaining Blue Seal certification.

indicators.text: Explain the responsibility of a business owner to employ individuals with various levels of training (e.g., apprentice, Red Seal or non-certified) and to provide quality customer service.

indicators.text: Outline an entry level business plan that may include start-up costs, location, customer base, advertising and an exit plan.

outcomes.statement: Apply proper handling of hazardous materials to prevent injury in the workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3E: Farm Chemical Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate the importance of, and methods used for, maintenance of a clean and safe workplace.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify important information categories from product labels, Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) and manufacturer's chemical information packages such as compatibility, storage requirements, application method, preharvest intervals and withdrawal periods.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the four parts of Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) (i.e., labels with warning symbols, hazard identification and product classification, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), worker education and worksite specific training).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the different hazards, identifiers and uses of consumer products, control products, and pesticides.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose and intended use of the mandatory information on a pesticide label as regulated by Health Canada.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the types of hazardous materials that an agricultural operation might create.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the potential heath risks of exposure to chemicals.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate record keeping strategies for maintaining SDS information.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore training and certification opportunities (e.g., WHMIS and pesticide applicator licence) on the safe use of agricultural chemicals.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the uses of agricultural chemicals that would require a Saskatchewan Pesticide Applicator Licence.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe handling of chemical products using approved safety gear.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Practise the safe storage of chemical products.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Develop procedures for handling mishaps such as chemical spills.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss first-aid procedures for exposure to agricultural chemicals (e.g., fertilizer, pesticide, fuel and anhydrous ammonia).

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Investigate regulations and responsibilities to safely dispose of leftover chemical and chemical containers.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Investigate the responsibilities and correct environmental handling, cleanup and waste disposal of cleaners, containers, coolants, filters, fuel and lubricants (e.g., grease and oil) including organizations that specialize in their cleanup.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Explore the environmental impacts of unsafe chemical waste disposal, and how that impacts Indigenous communities (e.g., water, animals and traditional medicinal plants).

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Practise the methods used to remove and dispose of chemical residue (e.g., fertilizer and pesticide spray) from application equipment.

indicators.text: Demonstrate the different hazards, identifiers and uses of consumer products, control products, and pesticides.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose and intended use of the mandatory information on a pesticide label as regulated by Health Canada.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the types of hazardous materials that an agricultural operation might create.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the potential heath risks of exposure to chemicals.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate record keeping strategies for maintaining SDS information.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore training and certification opportunities (e.g., WHMIS and pesticide applicator licence) on the safe use of agricultural chemicals.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the uses of agricultural chemicals that would require a Saskatchewan Pesticide Applicator Licence.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe handling of chemical products using approved safety gear.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Practise the safe storage of chemical products.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Develop procedures for handling mishaps such as chemical spills.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss first-aid procedures for exposure to agricultural chemicals (e.g., fertilizer, pesticide, fuel and anhydrous ammonia).

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Investigate regulations and responsibilities to safely dispose of leftover chemical and chemical containers.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Investigate the responsibilities and correct environmental handling, cleanup and waste disposal of cleaners, containers, coolants, filters, fuel and lubricants (e.g., grease and oil) including organizations that specialize in their cleanup.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Explore the environmental impacts of unsafe chemical waste disposal, and how that impacts Indigenous communities (e.g., water, animals and traditional medicinal plants).

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Practise the methods used to remove and dispose of chemical residue (e.g., fertilizer and pesticide spray) from application equipment.

outcomes.statement: Investigate employer and employee psychological health and safety in the workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6A: Psychological Health and Safety - Employer and Employee (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 5A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore accommodations (e.g., flexible hours, job sharing and modifications to the work environment and duties) that can be requested by employees of businesses in an agriculture setting (e.g., farming operations, chemical companies and grain elevators) to support mental health during peak operating efficiency.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss barriers (e.g., lack of awareness of accommodations, lack of confidence in requesting help, where to find supports, social stigma, fear of reprisal and fear of rejection) that employees face in disclosing a mental health problem or illness and/or requesting accommodations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe and suggest possible solutions for unavoidable stresses during peak operating times (e.g., harvest time, calving season and weather events) that employers face in providing accommodation requests.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss practical ways that employees can contribute to a psychologically healthy and safe workplace.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research employers' duties and responsibilities to support workplace mental health as outlined in The Saskatchewan Employment Act.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine employers' duty to accommodate employee requests as outlined in the Canadian Human Rights Code.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the current use of agriculture by Indigenous communities in Saskatchewan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7C: Contemporary Indigenous Agriculture (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 7B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore agricultural commodities produced in First Nations communities of Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the opportunities for growth that agriculture provides First Nations communities.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore programs that facilitate the development of agricultural enterprises among First Nations communities.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research current agricultural practices (e.g., Treaty Land Sharing Network) that honour treaty rights.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss Indigenous perspectives on the current and future use of agriculture in communities with an Elder or Knowledge Keeper.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore The Treaty Land Entitlement Framework Agreement and the impact it can have on indigenous agriculture.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the barriers (e.g., Treaty and government policies) that exist for Indigenous farmers that limit their farming operations on reserves.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify current programs specific to Indigenous agriculture.

outcomes.statement: Explore soil conservation and stewardship in sustainable agriculture production.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10C: Soil Management (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 10B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the relationship between sustainability and water and soil quality.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss Indigenous peoples' traditional values as they pertain to maintaining land and water health.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of historical and contemporary livestock and grain production practices that conserve water and maintain soil quality.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Research current methods (e.g., avoid overgrazing, cover crop and direct seeding) for reducing soil erosion.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the effectiveness of various farming methods (e.g., minimum tillage and crop rotation) for conserving soil health.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the key principles and practice of regenerative agriculture.

outcomes.statement: Explore the governing regulations and maintenance of livestock production facilities.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12C: Livestock Facility Regulations and Maintenance (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 12B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the facility requirements and regulations for different holding areas to separate animals for various reasons (e.g., breeding, egg laying, incubators, injured or ill animal, maternity pen and weaning).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the regulations and relevant calculations (e.g., animal unit month [AUM]) for determining suitable pasture size for a particular type and quantity of livestock.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Apply basic repair and maintenance skills to buildings, livestock facilities, vegetation and roads.

outcomes.statement: Prepare a management plan for a livestock operation of one or more specific species.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17B: Livestock Management Plan (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 7C, 10C and 17A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify one or more livestock species (e.g., cow/calf, dairy, equine, pork, bison, poultry and bees) for a farm operation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the provincial regulations and requirements for establishing a livestock operation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Determine the annual cycle (e.g., breeding and culling) and production cycle date ranges (e.g., postpartum, conception, mid gestation and late gestation) for the chosen livestock species.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the structures (e.g., buildings, fences and corrals) and land (e.g., features including soil types and use of that land) needed for a chosen livestock operation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze the suitability of farm locations for a chosen species of livestock and size of operation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate livestock management practices (e.g., percentage as meat processing, crossbreeding, show and aging livestock and introduction of new animals to the herd or operation) including the ability to handle waste (e.g., manure and carcasses) and herd protection measures (e.g., herd dogs, donkeys and structures).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Develop a nutrition program for a chosen species of livestock including sources of feed, prepared rations, feed storage, method of feeding, grazing methods and sources of water.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the finances of a chosen farm operation including human and equipment resources, types of products (e.g., meat, eggs, wool, honey and dairy) outsourcing stages (feedlot connection), accessibility to markets, cost of input and expected revenue.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss the implications of climate change (e.g., drought, deluge and storms) on the availability of feed and healthy pastures for grazing.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Prepare an effective time management schedule that balances farm time with school, work and recreation and considers seasonal time management differences.

outcomes.statement: Prepare a management plan for an operation of one or more specific species of crop.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18B: Crop Management Plan (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 7C, 10C and 18A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify specific crops (e.g., wheat, canola, lentils, fruit, vegetables and forage) for a farm operation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the advantages and disadvantages of a two-year, three-year, four-year and longer crop rotation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the influence of soil types, land features and climate on the choice of crop rotation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the buildings and equipment required for a chosen crop production operation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify the farming cycle date ranges for a chosen crop rotation (e.g., impact of spring and fall frost dates and the reasons for the order of crops in the rotation).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify planting methods for crops in a rotation (e.g., air seeder, planter and specialized seeder for forage crops).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify harvesting methods for crops in a rotation (e.g., swathing, baling, green chopping and straight cutting) and the advantages and disadvantages of using crop desiccation products.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain which fertilizers and chemicals can be used for a chosen crop rotation.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the process, advantages and disadvantages in applying chemicals (e.g., pre-plant, pre-emergence and post emergence) and fertilizers (e.g., broadcast, seed placed, mid row and side banded) to chosen crops.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Analyze the finances of a crop operation including seasonal workers, buy or lease equipment options, accessibility to markets, cost of input, cash input advances, crop insurance, forward contracting, the risks versus the advantages of forward contracting and expected revenue.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the implications of climate change (e.g., drought, deluge and storms) on the growth, harvesting and yield of crops.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Prepare an effective time management schedule that balances farm time with school, recreation and work and considers seasonal time management differences.

outcomes.statement: Prepare a management plan for an operation involving one or more specific crop and livestock species.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19: Multi-product Management Plan (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 17A and 18A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the benefits (e.g., grain to feed livestock, manure to fertilize crops and financial coverage when one operation is less successful) of having crop and livestock production in the same operation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the role of livestock in a mixed operation (e.g., nutrient cycle, feeding crops to build organic matter in soil and livestock grazing for weed control).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify one or more species of crops (e.g., wheat, barley, canola, lentils, fruits and vegetables) and livestock (e.g., cow/calf, dairy, equine, pork, bison, egg production and bee keeping) that are suitable for a mixed operation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the annual and production cycle date ranges for chosen crop and livestock species.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the structures (e.g., buildings, fences and corrals) and land (e.g., land features including soil types and use of that land) needed for a chosen mixed operation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze the suitability of farm locations (e.g., soil type, landforms and climate) for a chosen multi-product operation.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate livestock management practices (e.g., percentage as meat processing, crossbreeding and introduction of new animals), the handling of manure as fertilizer and herd protection measures (e.g., herd dogs, donkeys and structures).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a livestock nutrition program for a chosen multi-product operation, including the use of crops for feed, feed storage, method of feeding, grazing methods and sources of water.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify planting and harvesting methods for the crops grown in a chosen multi-product operation.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore the crop rotation best suited for a chosen multi-product operation.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Identify the fertilizers and chemicals to be used for crops in a chosen multi-product operation.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Discuss the financial considerations needed for a chosen multi-product operation including human and equipment resources, types of products, seasonal and foreign workers, buy or lease equipment options, outsourcing stages, accessibility to markets, cost of input, grazing / harvesting restrictions associated with specific chemicals that are used in weed, insect and disease control for crops and expected revenue.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Prepare an effective time management schedule that balances farm time with school, work and recreation and considers seasonal time management.

outcomes.statement: Explore transportation regulations including the movement of farm equipment and livestock on public roads.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 20: Transportation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the licensing, insurance and operator's qualifications for handling different types of farm equipment on private land and public roads.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the Ministry of Highways requirements (e.g., permits, restrictions such as width-height-length and weight, lighting, slow moving signs, clear visibility rules and escort vehicle requirements) to transport farm equipment, livestock and grain on provincial highways and roads.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the implications that seasonal road restrictions have on a farming operation (e.g., marketing and labor requirements).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the requirements or exemption status for agricultural equipment and vehicles in the transportation of dangerous goods.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine provincial and federal livestock transportation regulations (e.g., types of trailers, food and water requirements, manifest and the amount of time livestock can be hauled).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of a transportation logbook.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: List examples of tools and emergency equipment required on farm machinery while in transport on a public road.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe the dangers of overhead power lines when moving farm equipment.

outcomes.statement: Explore safe and humane methods of euthanizing livestock.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22D: Basic Handling - Euthanasia (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 20 and 22B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze the protocol (e.g., animal is to be relocated, euthanized or marketed) for conditions or diseases for which treatment is unsuccessful using regular efforts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore common untreatable diseases (e.g., rabies, bovine spongiform encephalopathy [BSE] and avian influenza) that may result in euthanizing an animal.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how to protect humans and herds from transmissible diseases.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Evaluate situations (e.g., broken leg, end of life cycle and suffering) in which euthanasia may be necessary.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine acceptable and unacceptable methods of euthanizing animals.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore situations (e.g., infectious disease) in which a veterinarian may be required to perform euthanasia.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe acceptable methods of carcass disposal.

outcomes.statement: Apply understanding of nutrition to livestock feeding programs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23C: Livestock Feeding Programs (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 23B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the function of parts of the digestive system and the concept of rumination in specific livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of different types of feeding systems.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Investigate support programs for managing livestock feeding.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop and use feeding and nutritional records.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Determine the cost of feed (e.g., hay, grain and supplements) for one animal of a specific type of livestock, for one year.

indicators.label: g

outcomes.statement: Explore the function of specialized equipment used in livestock operations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24C: Specialized Equipment for Livestock (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the function of equipment used in the honey extraction process (e.g., scratcher, de-capping tool, extractor, separator, settling tanks, pumps, melter).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the importance of specialized equipment (e.g., piglet heating equipment, ventilation and cooler systems) in a swine production facility.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the ban of gestation crates in Canada.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the function of equipment (e.g., milking machine, pasteurizers, separators, homogenizers and tanks) used in the milking process in dairy farming.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the tools (e.g., clippers, shears, carding paddles, roving machine) used to shear sheep and turn their fur into yarn.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the function of equipment (e.g., incubators, hatchery equipment, egg transfer machines, slaughter equipment) used on a fowl farm and/or egg production facility.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the individual mechanical components (e.g., rollers, motors) in feed mills.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the equipment used to remove animal waste from housing facilities and spreading or injecting the waste as fertilizer.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the use of medication in treating livestock.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25C: Livestock Health Care - Medication (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 25B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the medical treatment of common diseases (e.g., white muscle disease, bovine black leg and foot rot) in livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the function and use of anaesthetics, antibiotics and vaccines.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the relationship between drug withdrawal time and maximum drug residue limits in the body or products of an animal (e.g., milk, eggs and honey).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research Health Canada regulations that prescribe acceptable residue levels of medication in livestock and livestock products.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze the storage, handling and disposal of medications in a drug protocol and medication program for a livestock operation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the manufacturer's specifications for dosage of medications to ensure optimum effectiveness.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine treatment options to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain why different injection sites are used for vaccines and antibiotics.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify the location on an animal to administer a particular antibiotic or vaccine.

indicators.label: j
k
indicators.text: Investigate the economic considerations of using medications (e.g., medication cost versus value of animal).

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of maintaining livestock health history records.

outcomes.statement: Explore the regulations governing livestock products and the impact of livestock products in secondary industries.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 26B: Livestock Products - Secondary Industries (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 8

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the regulations governing the production of a specific animal food product.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify grading requirements for a specific product.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how animal products are used to create secondary industries (e.g., leather in clothing manufacturing, beeswax in candles and gelatin for cheese) in the marketplace.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the impact of secondary industries on the economic value of livestock products.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify local, provincial, national and international markets for various products.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore how livestock products can be the focus or supplemental income of a farming operation.

outcomes.statement: Explore effective pasture stocking, weed control and financial management practices.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27C: Pasture – Management (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 10C and 27A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze the importance of stocking rates on livestock health and pasture sustainability.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe strategies of using livestock for noxious weed and invasive plant control (e.g., goat and sheep grazing).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the benefits and environmental impact of various grazing strategies (e.g., intensive, rotational, swath and spring/fall) on tame and native prairie.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the stocking rates for tame and native prairie including animal unit month (AUM) calculations.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the management of species at risk that use pastures as their habitat.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the costs (e.g., rate of gain, forage production, taxes and fencing) of grazing cattle.

outcomes.statement: Explore livestock records.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 28C: Livestock Record Keeping - Planning and Analysis (Optional) · Suggested Time: 8-12 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 28B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how records can be used to communicate between people (e.g., employers and employees, co-workers, veterinarians, feed specialists and end consumers) involved in the farming operation.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Explore how collected data is analyzed to inform necessary changes to the production operation.

outcomes.statement: Explore crop records.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 29C: Crop Record Keeping - Planning and Analysis (Optional) · Suggested Time: 8-12 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 29B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how records can be used to communicate between people (e.g., employers and employees, co-workers, grain specialists, agrologists, suppliers and end consumers) involved in a farming operation.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Explore how collected data is analyzed to inform necessary changes to the production operation.

outcomes.statement: Investigate care of pregnant and post-birth livestock.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 30B: Reproduction - Pregnancy (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the factors to consider regarding management of a pregnant female including gestation period, expected birthing date, health care, labour and post-birthing care.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the different methods used to help an animal give birth (e.g., pulling and caesarian-section).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify delivery situations that require veterinary care (e.g., breech, lengthy labour and mother in distress).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the characteristics, treatment and prevention of common metabolic conditions (e.g., ketosis, milk fever and mastitis) associated with reproduction.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the basic care of newborn livestock.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the use of milk replacer, replacement mother and proper facilities (e.g., special pens, milk bottles and/or feed and water containers) to care for orphaned offspring.

outcomes.statement: Explore the management of an organic livestock operation.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 32C: Organic Livestock Production - Management (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 32B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the sources and types of organic feed required for specific livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the prohibited substances that cannot be included in organic feed.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare the required timing of organic feed for specific livestock (e.g., during their entire life or starting well after birth).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the breeding requirements of organic livestock.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the traceability of livestock products to prove organic status.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research how organic farm operations prepare for an inspection.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the economic considerations of transitioning to organic livestock production (e.g., barn modifications, pasture requirements and cost of organic feed).

outcomes.statement: Explore the management of organic crop production.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 33C: Organic Crop Production - Management (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 33B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the standards and regulations for organic crop production as determined by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the traceability of crop products to prove organic status.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research how organic farm operations prepare for an inspection.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the process that is involved in transitioning to organic farming including economic considerations (e.g., crop yield and crop price).

outcomes.statement: Explore the production of plant protein by producers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 36B: Plant Protein - Production (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 36A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the benefit of including pulse crops in crop rotation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the suitability of different soil types in producing plant-based or animal-based protein.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research how producers are improving the quality of protein feedstock derived from Saskatchewan crops.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze the energy and resource cost for creating one pound of protein from animals compared to plants.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Debate the advantages and disadvantages of using genetically modified organisms (GMOs) to increase plant protein levels.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the impact of plant protein production on, and Canada's role in, global food sustainability.

outcomes.statement: Explore the use of pesticides, herbicides, fungicides and desiccants.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 37B: Crop Health Care - Pesticides, Herbicides, Fungicides and Desiccants (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 3C

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify various pests, weeds and diseases that could occur in cereal, pulse and oilseed crop rotations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify beneficial insects that may be found in a cereal, pulse, oilseed rotation and the pests they attack.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the economic thresholds for various diseases and insect infestations in a pulse, cereal and oilseed rotation.

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the concept of biosecurity and how it relates to protecting crops.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze advantages and disadvantages of various product application methods (e.g., seed treatments, high clearance sprayer and aerial application).

indicators.label: h

indicators.label: i

indicators.label: j

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: f

indicators.label: g

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80C: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III - Occupational Health and Safety in n The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019.
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse - work that you believe is unusually dangerous

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one's performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Examine the impact of colonization and government policies and practices on Indigenous food sovereignty.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Indigenous Food Sovereignty (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore traditional Indigenous food sourcing practices.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare food sourcing practices of traditional Indigenous, early settler and present-day communities.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the importance of country foods and wild-harvested foods in traditional and contemporary Indigenous communities.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the historical and current impact of the Indian Act on Indigenous agricultural practices in Canada.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the impact of government policies, including the reserve system, and the Peasant Farm Policy, and practices, including the pass system and home farm program, on historical and contemporary Indigenous agricultural practices.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Summarize the impact of prairie colonization and the reserve system on Indigenous food sovereignty.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate agricultural and food sourcing initiatives currently underway on various Saskatchewan First Nations to achieve food sovereignty.

outcomes.statement: Assess the environmental, economic and social impacts of food loss and food waste.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Food Loss and Food Waste (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 7

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between food loss and food waste.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research factors that can contribute to food loss (e.g., pests attacking a crop, animal deaths, transportation issues) and food waste (e.g., purchasing or preparing more food than can be consumed, inadequate storage).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research traditional Indigenous approaches to food efficiency, food waste and food loss.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify measures the Canadian agriculture industry takes to reduce or prevent food loss, including protection from loss to pests, spoilage and advances in processing and transportation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Define the term upcycling as it pertains to by-products of food and reduction of food waste.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the redirection of unusable and unwanted food from the human food stream into food for animals.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare Canadian food waste and food loss data to that of a country in the developing world and speculate on reasons for differences.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of curbing food loss and food waste to help address global food insecurity.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain the difference between “best before” and “expiry” date labels on purchased foods.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Develop a plan for reducing personal food waste (e.g., shopping with a grocery list, finding new ways to use leftovers, meal planning, freezing foods).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Investigate organizations dedicated to reducing food waste in Saskatchewan and Canada.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Propose actions (e.g., donating unsold fresh goods to local charities, educating consumers on ways to cut household food waste, implementing employee education programs) that retailers such as grocery stores, bakeries and restaurants can take to curb food waste.

outcomes.statement: Examine the influence of media and marketing on consumer food choices.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Media and Marketing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify sources (e.g., social media, newspaper, television, word of mouth) available to the Canadian public for information on the agriculture and food industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess the importance of, and ways to determine, the credibility of a source of information.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine forms of food marketing such as branding, product packaging, event sponsorship, celebrity endorsements, contests and sales promotions, social media posts, commercials and product placement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify personal data (e.g., age, gender, online purchasing and web browsing history) that can be harnessed for targeted marketing of food and other products.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the role of social media influencers and bloggers in food marketing, considering the potential benefits and challenges associated with their influence on consumer behavior and public trust in agriculture.

indicators.label: f
g
h
indicators.text: Suggest actions that individual consumers can undertake to influence the retail food sector in Canada.

outcomes.statement: Assess the impact of technology and innovation on agricultural production in Saskatchewan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Technology and Innovation (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 10

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the role of research and development in agricultural innovation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between natural selection, traditional plant breeding and scientific genetic manipulation in crops.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the role of data analytics and farm management software in decision-making processes, including yield prediction, disease monitoring, and real-time monitoring of crop and soil conditions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the history of technology and innovation, including automation, in Saskatchewan agriculture.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate current application of innovative machine technology and crop and plant science biotechnology in Saskatchewan agriculture.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the current state and emerging opportunities associated with digital agriculture in Saskatchewan and Canada.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Summarize reasons for innovation in Saskatchewan’s agriculture sector.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe the relationship between agriculture biotechnology and food system sustainability.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate the purpose of, and benefits derived from, Saskatchewan’s Global Institute for Food Security.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the importance of digital agriculture to sustainable food systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Digital Agriculture (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 11

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the characteristics of digitally assisted precision agriculture.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain potential environmental and economic benefits of digitally assisted precision agriculture.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research current technological innovations used in digitally assisted precision agriculture, such as Global Positioning Systems [GPS], precision machinery and drones.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore emerging trends and future directions in digital agriculture, such as artificial intelligence, robotics, and autonomous farming systems, and their potential impacts on farm productivity.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Assess how various types of digital farm data informs the management of small areas within fields (e.g., effective application of fertilizers, pesticides, tillage and irrigation water).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss issues (e.g., ownership, security, control) related to farming data.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research challenges and opportunities encountered by a farming operation that implements digitally assisted precision agriculture.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the role of digitally assisted precision agriculture in supporting sustainable food systems.

outcomes.statement: Assess the importance of animal health and well-being to sustainable food systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Animal Health and Well-being (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 10

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between animal health and animal well-being.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss animal welfare as a human responsibility.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the concept of biosecurity and its role in preventing the introduction and spread of diseases in livestock populations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the Five Freedoms (i.e., freedom from hunger and thirst; freedom from discomfort; freedom from pain, injury, and disease; freedom to express normal and natural behavior [e.g., having sufficient space]; and freedom from fear and distress) as the globally recognized gold standard in animal welfare.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how voluntary and mandatory assurance systems (e.g., Verified Beef Production Plus and proAction), can assure consumers that animal welfare standards are being maintained.

indicators.label: f
g
indicators.text: Identify the role of organizations such as the National Farm Animal Care Council, Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Canadian Cattle Association/Saskatchewan Cattleman’s Association, Saskatchewan Ministry of Agriculture, Saskatchewan Stock Growers Association, Saskatchewan Egg Producers, Dairy Farmers of Saskatchewan/Canada, Canadian Cervid Alliance, Chicken Farmers of Saskatchewan and the Saskatchewan Pork Development Board in advocating for the health and welfare of animals raised for food in Saskatchewan and Canada.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess essential elements (e.g., adequate ventilation and space, proper drainage, access to food and water) of animal welfare during transportation of livestock.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain the importance of animal health in supporting sustainable food systems.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Evaluate current federal and provincial laws and regulations for animal health and welfare. (e.g., Federal Health of Animals Act, Saskatchewan Animal Protection Act and Regulations 2018, Saskatchewan Animal Health Act 2019).

outcomes.statement: Develop a plan for starting a school or community garden.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18A: Community and School Gardens A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 17

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research how community gardens operate locally and elsewhere in the province.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the potential benefits (e.g., health, social, economic, cultural) and challenges (e.g., conflicts among users, competition for resources) often associated with community gardens.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore potential opportunities and challenges associated with a school garden.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research information on growing a healthy garden.

indicators.label: e

outcomes.statement: Implement a plan for a school or community garden.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18B: Community and School Gardens B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 20-25 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 18A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of monitoring and documenting the operations and progress of a garden.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify life skills gained through gardening.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Implement a school or community garden plan.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Monitor plan progress and make adjustments as required throughout the life of the garden.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on personal and collective successes and challenges resulting from the implementation of the garden plan.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Predict how gardening can contribute to food security.

outcomes.statement: Assess personal suitability and interest in agriculture and food sector careers.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on personal values, interests, skills, personality traits, aptitude and abilities.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the range of career opportunities available in the agriculture and food sectors provincially, nationally and internationally (e.g., farming or food production, agritourism, research, animal health and welfare, advocacy and policy).

indicators.text: Conduct informational interviews with individuals employed in the agriculture and food sectors to gain firsthand information about their career journeys (e.g., crop or livestock production, agribusiness, food processing and distribution, crop and animal science, research, health and safety).

e
indicators.text: Assess personal suitability for one or more careers in the agriculture and food sector.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a career journey plan that supports a preferred future in the agriculture and food sector.
