indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i

indicators.label: j

indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: h

allEvidence.observation: Each entry on the course's outcomes page is one module: the entry is titled with the module name and shows a “Module Code” (the outcome code in sk.json); the module's own page prints one “Outcome” with its indicators. outcomes.statement: Use world theatre traditions to inspire ideas for own dramatic work.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate how performance styles (e.g. mask, storytelling, shadow puppetry, naturalism, commedia) inform ideas.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate how different styles have been applied to traditional plays (e.g., Macbeth adaptation to Pawâkan Macbeth).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Organize and document ideas for possible exploration (e.g., portfolio, journal, digital media).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Devise and perform dramatic work inspired by world theatre traditions.

outcomes.statement: Create dramatic work demonstrating use of genre and style.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research style or genre and share learning (e.g., design a student-led workshop, act out a scene).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Incorporate and justify the use of genre and style in own devised work.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Select an aspect of theory and/or style and apply to own work through, for example:
- improvised play
- performance art
- monologue
- scene
- video

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Juxtapose unlike genre and style (e.g., use puppets to explore a political issue, create a Victorian ‘drawing room play’ using social media as script).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Design the look and sound of a scene to reflect a genre or style (e.g., director’s notebook, sketches, production notes, maquette, set list).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the strengths of the drama work and/or performance and reflect on the collaborative approaches, challenges, and individual contributions encountered in the creative process.

outcomes.statement: Express a multiplicity of voices and perspectives (e.g., self, family, community, marginalized individuals, silenced people in history, powerful figures, celebrities, extraterrestrials, fictional characters) through works of dramatic art.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Assume roles in order to represent a variety of voices and perspectives.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: When preparing a scene, monologue or play, consider questions such as: whose voice and perspective is being heard? Who is left out of the story? How does voice impact the story? How does the perspective impact the audience?

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze and describe how personal identity and cultural lens affects creation of the work.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore ways of expressing power, status and perspective through drama work (e.g., Image Theatre, Forum Theatre, contextual drama).

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate directorial choices for a performance that utilizes oral or written text and/or devised material.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Collaborate with peers, Elders or community experts to decide on the merits of various creative processes for building a specific drama work (e.g., play, collective creation, devised theatre, performance art).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Work with peers to select a creative process and make a production plan (e.g., roles, budget, timelines, expectations).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Develop source material (e.g., analyze and/or decode text, image, sound, movement, research, story, idea) and build the drama work within the selected process.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Construct and revise the rehearsal process according to the style and needs of the production.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Engage, where possible, with Saskatchewan directors about their own creative processes (e.g., interview, research, email, view or listen online).

outcomes.statement: Present and sustain a performance for an audience (e.g., peers, invited guests, public) that demonstrates innovation (e.g., aesthetic and technical).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Purposefully use the language of theatre in selected creative processes.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Practically explore the director’s toolbox (e.g., communication of vision, interpretation of oral or written text, analysis and planning, creating a rehearsal plan) for artistic purpose.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Reinterpret or imagine a scene or dramatic work through innovative use of various theatrical toolboxes (e.g., director, designer, actor).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use a specific technical component (e.g., light, costume, sound, digital technologies) for symbolic purposes as a mode for communicating ideas.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Change the point of view of a scene or dramatic work by amplifying a technical or artistic aspect (e.g., incorporate contact improv, actor and audience interaction, replace the actor with an object or technical component, project digital images on moving actors, use social media conventions in performance).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate willingness to take creative risks.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Justify decisions made by various roles (e.g., director, actor, designer) to achieve intent.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on problems, surprises or challenges that arose in the performance and how they might be resolved.

outcomes.statement: Respond critically, using appropriate theatrical language, to directorial choices in a variety of performance experiences (e.g., live, digital).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: View and reflect on a live or recorded performance and discuss the role of the audience in various types of performances (e.g., conventional Western theatre, children’s theatre, forum theatre, site specific).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the differences and similarities between staged theatre and plays adapted to film.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Review and reflect on directorial choices in various genres of recorded and/or live theatre.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: View a filmed adaptation of a play and identify the qualities specific to film that cannot be replicated on stage and the qualities of staged performance that cannot be replicated through film.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss considerations a director makes when creating a film adaptation such as location, setting, directing the viewer’s focus through camera angles and shots, special effects, computer generated imagery (CGI) and editing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on the impact of directorial choices on an audience and one’s own experiences viewing plays.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Recognize the effect the location of the theatre has on the audience, such as outdoor theatre, theatre in the round, site-specific theatre, historical theatres.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore several different ways to critique (e.g., written, verbal, collage, multimedia, journal, monologue) using language specific to theatre or film.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss how viewing theatre shapes future decisions in making theatre.

outcomes.statement: Examine the purpose of theatre in societies.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Interview a member of a professional or community-based theatre company about their vision, focus and process (e.g., How do you determine your season? How do you promote your work? How do you get funding? How do you develop a budget? How do you recoup costs?).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a vision and focus for an imagined theatre company.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Develop an outline to describe an imagined theatre company (e.g., name, company members, season schedule, budget and location).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create a proposal, including sponsorship and funding plan (e.g., social media, PR and publicity, logo).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Pitch a proposal for a production, season or grant and defend the proposal to a panel of peers.

outcomes.statement: Research and experiment with contemporary theatre practices.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss connections between Indigenous artistic traditions (e.g., song, dance, stories) and the land, identity and worldview.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize how artistic practices can be specific to a treaty territory, cultural and/or language group in Saskatchewan and Canada (e.g., examine drama and theatre traditions of newcomer students’ communities, treaty education outcome TPP12 - represent personal understanding of the concept, We Are All Treaty People).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research and examine how past traditions inform contemporary theatre.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create a maquette or theatrical diagram of modern production choices for a play.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the impact and contributions of contemporary theatre practitioners working within various theatre roles (e.g., writers, dramaturge, performers, directors, stage managers, designers of set/costume/lighting/sound, choreographers of fight/dance, music directors/musicians, technicians).

outcomes.statement: Examine the role of the theatre and artists as potential agents of social change.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze and practically explore a theatre movement that arose in response to social conditions (e.g., Paper Wheat in response to the creation of farming cooperatives in Saskatchewan, Native Earth Performing Arts in response to colonialism, Theatre of the Absurd in Europe and Butoh in Japan in response to WWII, Guerrilla Theatre in response to radical social movements of the 1960s, Bread and Puppets in the 1970s in response to social activism in USA).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Practically explore a current social issue of interest (e.g., treaty education outcome TR12, indicator - analyze how the media currently depicts the treaty relationship and determine the effects this has on public perception, marginalized groups, issues identified in the media) and consider how one might respond through dramatic work.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine how theatre artists use their art form to question the status quo and empower others to influence change (e.g., challenging perspectives on gender equity).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry to examine Saskatchewan theatres and theatre artists (e.g., Gordon Tootoosis Nikaniwin Theatre, SUM Theatre, Persephone Theatre, Globe Theatre, Dancing Sky Theatre, Troupe du Jour, Curtain Razors, Listen to Dis, Deaf Crows, Live Five) whose work addresses local and/or global issues (e.g., food security, water access, health, migration, colonization, reconciliation, climate change, gender and sexual diversity, ethics and technologies, economic disparity, economic, social and environmental sustainability).

outcomes.statement: Research contemporary and/or current theatre practices of First Nations, Inuit and Métis artists in Canada.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss questions concerning the relationship between identity and art-making practices (e.g., Does culture influence the subject matter or themes of dramatic work? How might traditional practices inform the work of specific artists?).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Conduct research on a contemporary First Nations, Inuit or Métis theatre company in Canada and report on such things as company philosophy or focus, subject or themes presented, discipline specific or interdisciplinary approaches and/or the potential influence of local cultural practices.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research (e.g., in person interviews, written information, recorded or online interview) an Indigenous theatre artist and examine what impacts his or her work, considering questions such as What is the role of Indigenous theatre in the local community and society? Is it important to distinguish Indigenous theatre separately from non-Indigenous theatre? Does cultural identity influence the work?

indicators.label: c

indicators.label: f

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate the roles of society in ensuring the safety of children (e.g., Amber Alerts).

outcomes.statement: Explore theories and risk factors related to early childhood mental health.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 26: Mental Health Theories and Risk Factors for Children (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 25

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore brain development from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate key developmental theories related to infant and early mental health, such as attachment, resilience and emotional regulation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Research how children’s mental health and development outcomes are impacted by the following factors:
- child factors (e.g., pre-and postnatal experiences and circumstances, temperament);
- socio-demographic and societal factors (e.g., community, environment, level of income); and,
- parental or caregiver factors (e.g., consistency, parenting attitudes and styles).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how to promote secure attachment relationships in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research trauma-sensitive care practices.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize potential causes of stress and anxiety for young children (e.g., moving, separation, residual trauma).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Distinguish the three levels of stress (i.e., positive, tolerable, toxic) and their impact on child development.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the impact of stress on brain development, including prenatal and postpartum experiences.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Determine early indicators (e.g., withdrawal behaviour, compulsive activities, loss of earlier developmental achievements) of mental health disorders in young children.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify local organizations that support mental health for young children and their families (e.g., Saskatchewan Prevention Institute).

outcomes.statement: Describe how early learning and child care caregivers can develop positive relationships with families and the community.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27: Relationships With Children’s Families (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the benefits of strong collaborative partnerships between early learning and child care caregivers and childrens’ families.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify barriers to positive relations between early learning and child care caregivers and childrens’ families.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss ways to include families in planning activities, supports and resources when appropriate.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe strategies that can improve relationships and communications between caregivers and children’s families (e.g., communication apps, daily verbal reports).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how parents, guardians and families are the experts on their child.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify ways to recognize, respect and incorporate family strengths (e.g., highlighting what is strong rather that what is wrong, confirming things they know they are doing well) when interacting with families.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare a variety of community resources for families with young children.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research facilities (e.g., libraries, family resource centres, community centres) and events (e.g., festivals, theatre, dance, music, sport) that build relationships in the community.

outcomes.statement: Determine ways to support children’s culture, identity and sense of belonging.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 28: Children’s Culture and Identity (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss what it means to belong to a family and a community (e.g., birthplace, name, parents, grandparents and community connections).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize how connection to others, place and language influence identity development.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate ways to ensure parents, guardians and families feel included and have a sense of belonging in early learning environments.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate ways to include families’ cultural identities in early learning and child care environments (e.g., books, posters, family pictures, orally transmitted stories, decorations, music).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research ways in which early learning and child care environments can support language learning (e.g., through music, literacy, vocabulary building activities).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify ways to support and foster identity when working with young children (e.g., selecting multilingual books and software, selecting music of various genres that reflect the local contemporary cultural community, using manipulatives and loose parts familiar to the children, learning key words in children’s home language).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe strategies that can be used in early learning and child care environments to challenge gender stereotypes.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research local events of social, ceremonial and community activities available to families with young children.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate protocols for inviting grandparents, family members, Knowledge Keepers or Elders into an early learning setting to share stories, songs, dances or cultural foods.

outcomes.statement: Explore Indigenous approaches to child rearing, nurturing and learning.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 29: Indigenous Approaches to Child Rearing (Core for Early Learning Pathway) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research traditional Indigenous prenatal supports, delivery and postpartum care programs available in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Engage with a local First Nations or Métis Elder to talk about traditional early child development teachings.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore cultural teachings related to birth and infancy.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the role of grandparents and Elders in raising children (e.g., transmitting language, ceremony and culture, teaching stories, role modeling).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate kinship relationships and roles of family and community members (e.g., aunties, uncles, stepparents, parents-in-law, existing natural supports) in caring for Indigenous children.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the importance of ancestral language development in traditional approaches to child rearing, nurturing, and learning.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of spending time on the land with young children to support the development of their identity.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the importance of pregnancy, children and older persons in Indigenous communities.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research tipi teachings and how they are applicable to nurturing and development.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify local agencies that can support learning about traditional Indigenous teachings.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research the impact of residential schools, the Sixties Scoop and the millennial scoop on the physical, mental, emotional and spiritual connections between children, parents, families and communities.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the principles of learning through play and exploration.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 30: Play and Exploration (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Determine the functions of play (e.g., express personal thoughts and feelings, develop self-control, assess risks, develop language and literacy skills).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate Parten’s levels of play (i.e., uninvolved, onlooker, solitary, parallel, associative, cooperative) and the risks of social play.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Observe examples of atypical play to determine the need for further intervention.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the role of play in brain development.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the role of adults as part of the play process (e.g., modeling oral language and emergent literacy, providing props and resources to enrich play, observing children’s play to assess social and cognitive growth).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how adults support safe play (e.g., interrupt and intervene when necessary, watch for safety, differentiate between a risk and a hazard during roughhousing).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare guided play (e.g., when adults participate in play) and free play (e.g., when children engage in self-directed play).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the different types of play schemas (e.g., connection, transformation, trajectory, rotation, envelopment).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Categorize age-appropriate loose parts according to the different types of play schemas (e.g., tape for connecting, spray bottles for transforming, fabrics for enveloping).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Evaluate toys intended for infants, toddlers and preschoolers according to specific criteria such as safety and developmental appropriateness.

outcomes.statement: Explore the physical domain of development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31: Physical Domain of Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Distinguish the differences between gross motor skills (e.g., laterality, spatial awareness, left/right dominance, balance) and fine motor skills (e.g., handedness, coordination, dexterity) from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the benefits of physical activity for young children (e.g., develops strength, flexibility and endurance, maintain healthy weight, lowers stress and anxiety).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Plan experiences that allow children to develop fine motor skills and represent their learning (e.g., manipulating small objects) for different age groupings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss indoor structures, spaces and equipment (e.g., climbing structures, space to dance, balls, scarves) that promote large muscle development for different age groupings.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create a safe obstacle course or balance trail for different age groupings in which toddlers and preschoolers use loco motor skills such as walking, running, skipping, rolling or maintaining balance.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Design an activity or game for different age groupings designed to develop manipulative skills such as throwing, tossing, kicking, catching or striking.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Design an activity or game for different age groupings designed to develop an awareness of space by adjusting their movements around furniture, objects, hazards, adults and children in a common space.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate strategies to develop healthy habits independently (e.g., wearing a bicycle helmet) when engaging in free play.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Develop a template to observe the physical developmental skills of a child in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss how children’s physical development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore the social-emotional domain of development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 32: Social-Emotional Domain of Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 31

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore aspects related to the social-emotional domain of development (e.g. developing self-concept and self-esteem, regulating emotions, interacting with others) from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore self-awareness including name, favourite personal traits, interests, favourite food, extra-curricular activities, community and cultural connections.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research culturally appropriate ways to provide support to children who have difficulty separating from family.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Role play a scene in which an early learning and child care caregiver models strategies to identify and regulate emotions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Model strategies, for different age groupings, to consider the perspective of others and show empathy.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a template to observe the social and emotional growth of a child in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how social-emotional development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore the intellectual domain of development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 33: Intellectual Domain of Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 32

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore aspects of the intellectual domain of development (e.g., creating and imagining, recognizing attributes and characteristics, exploring numeracy, language and literacy) from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research creative representations, constructions or props to encourage imaginative play for toddlers and preschoolers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Curate a selection of open-ended age-appropriate materials, including culturally relevant materials, (e.g., loose parts such as shells, pine cones, small stones, fabrics, wood materials, beads, water containers, clay, tools and utensils) that children can use to recognize attributes and characteristics.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify a selection of age-appropriate tools and devices (e.g., measuring tapes, measuring cups, rulers, sticks) children can use for measurement.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the presence of numeracy in everyday life in an early learning setting (e.g., counting songs, estimating amounts, measuring lengths).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify age-appropriate activities to explore the concept of time (e.g., posting a calendar, talking about seasons, planning long-term multi-step projects).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Create age-appropriate activities to explore positioning (e.g. before, after, over, under, in front, behind).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a template to observe the intellectual developmental skills of a child in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss how intellectual development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore the spiritual domain of development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 34: Spiritual Domain of Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 33

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe a memory of sensory perceptions related to the beauty and wonder of the world experienced as a young child.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine what captures the attention, engages the senses and triggers possible emotions after walking or spending time outside.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss ways to safely expose infants, toddlers and preschoolers to the natural world.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate opportunities to explore the senses using natural and culturally relevant materials such as interesting textures to touch (e.g., feathers, pebbles, sticks), smell (e.g. spices, plants, herbs), see (e.g. coloured beads, flowers, birds, mirrors) and hear (e.g. music, wind chimes, instruments).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Brainstorm vocabulary to describe textures, sounds, smells, colours or tastes.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how spiritual development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore language and literacy development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 35: Language and Literacy Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 34

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore aspects related to language and literacy development (e.g., engaging in conversation, exploring words, representing ideas) from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss how language can be developed through interactions in play.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify opportunities for children to listen with engagement (e.g., musical performances, puppet shows, stories, visits from Elders and grandparents).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate age-appropriate strategies to introduce new vocabulary in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate asking complex questions (e.g., “How does that work?”, “Why do leaves change colors?”) rather than simple questions (e.g., “What’s that?” or “Where are we going?”).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research songs, poems and books with texts that rhyme, use alliterations and explore different sounds.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate interactive reading with individuals or small groups (e.g., reading with expression, articulating clearly, inviting comments, asking for predictions, sharing feelings and experiences).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze representations of ideas created by children (e.g., drawing, painting, collage, construction, dramatic play).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research the benefits of bilingualism or multilingualism in early childhood.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Investigate how young children learn additional languages (e.g., extended time period to acquire the additional language and build confidence, exploration and play with peers and adults, singing familiar and repetitive songs).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss ways to support the use and development of home language.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Curate a selection of language and literacy materials (e.g., songs, rhymes, books) that are connected to cultures, home languages and familial understandings in the community.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Develop a template to observe children’s language and literacy skills related to the intellectual developmental domain.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss how language and literacy development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore observation, documentation and assessment processes in early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 36: Observation, Documentation and Assessment (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between observation, documentation and assessment.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Investigate developmentally appropriate and culturally responsive assessment practices, such as developing a relationship with the child, administering assessment tools in the child’s first language and allowing children to represent their ideas in a variety of ways.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between screening tools (e.g., observation templates, journals, data collection, notes) and assessment tools (e.g. early years assessments).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore specialized assessments completed by professional specialists (e.g., speech language pathologist, occupational therapist, educational psychologist).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Evaluate documentation tools (e.g., pictures, videos, products) used to record the four domains of development.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate appropriate ways (e.g., terminology) to discuss children’s learning and development amongst colleagues or with parents and guardians.

outcomes.statement: Investigate characteristics of an inclusive early learning program.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 37: Inclusive Early Learning Programs (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 36

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Compare a medical model of supporting children with diverse abilities (i.e., focus on diagnosis) to a holistic needs-based model (i.e., focus on strengths, abilities and needs of the child).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe strategies for responsive teaching such as making evidence-based decisions, valuing relationships and meeting students’ needs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe exceptionalities that may require intensive supports (e.g., visual impairment, deafness, autism spectrum disorder).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate adaptations (e.g., in learning centres or invitations for learning, daily activities and routines) for children needing targeted and intensive supports.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss adaptations (e.g., in learning centres or invitations for learning, daily activities and routines) for children needing universal supports.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the role of the early learning and child care caregiver in documenting and reporting for early intervention (e.g., observe, screen and monitor child development).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how to collaborate with other professionals and families to develop a holistic understanding of the child.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate how to conduct strengths-based interventions (e.g., acknowledging skills, knowledge, talents, character traits, relationships and abilities rather than deficits).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate the use of talking circles when planning an intervention.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research specialized professions related to early childhood development (e.g., occupational therapist, speech therapist, child psychologist, behaviour therapist, physiotherapist).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Evaluate an indoor and an outdoor environment for children with diverse abilities.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Research local and provincial organizations that offer specialized supports (e.g., Inclusion Saskatchewan, Autism Support Services, Saskatchewan Alternate Format Materials Library, Early Childhood Intervention Program, Kids First, Saskatchewan Prevention Institute).

outcomes.statement: Create an invitation for learning.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 38: Invitations for Learning (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-12 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 17, 22, 28, 30 and 36

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define invitations for learning (i.e., a collection of interesting and carefully combined materials that may be used in a number of ways to draw children’s attention).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare thematic planning to child-guided planning.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss preferred ways to present invitations (e.g., visually appealing presentation, materials that define the space, intentional positioning of the objects).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore considerations for designing invitations (e.g., the textures, smells, sounds, materials that change when manipulated or combined, the amount of materials for the number of children, cultural relevancy).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Observe children engaging with an invitation to determine ways to extend learning and play.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine invitations that promote literacy and language development.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore materials that could be used in outdoor invitations (e.g., hub caps, hay bales, steering wheels, pieces of wood).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate ways invitations could be used to support the cultures of children in the program.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore how play schemas and their corresponding loose parts can be incorporated into invitations.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Plan an invitation for learning, including the budget for materials.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Create an invitation for learning for a targeted age grouping (e.g., toddlers, preschoolers).

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Evaluate the efficacy of the invitation for learning.

outcomes.statement: Examine the structure of the Canadian health care system.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 41: Canadian Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research historical aspects of Medicare in Canada and how it has evolved.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Interpret the five principles of Medicare as listed in the Canada Health Act.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify federal, provincial and territorial roles in the Canadian health care system.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate among primary, secondary and tertiary health care deliveries.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the advantages and disadvantages of private and publicly funded health care services.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare the Canadian determinants of health with the World Health Organization determinants of health.

outcomes.statement: Investigate health care services for First Nations, Métis and Inuit people in Canada.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 43: Indigenous Health Care (Core For Supportive Care Focus) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 41

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Summarize the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada’s Calls to Action related to health (e.g., numbers 18-24).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the origins of the relationship between federal health services and First Nations and Métis people (e.g., Treaty negotiations, Northern Intertribal Health Authority).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the Non-insured Health Benefits Program for First Nations peoples registered under the Indian Act.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore Métis, Non-Status and Inuit health coverage in Canada.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the historical significance of Jordan’s Principle and the impact on health services.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate how the federal and provincial governments collaborate to provide funding for First Nations to access health care.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore access to health care in remote areas.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate issues related to diabetes in Indigenous communities.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore health care clauses in the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP) Act related to Bill C-15.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research options for First Nations to choose health self-governance in Canada.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Investigate ways of actualizing the roles of Indigenous Elders and Knowledge Keepers in the health care system.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the work environment of acute care settings.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 45: Acute Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 40

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate acute care.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the challenges of working in acute care as a supportive care provider.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the supportive care provider’s responsibilities for physical examinations (e.g., collect linens, collect examination equipment, measure vital signs).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the different types of surgeries (i.e., elective, urgent, emergency) and their purposes (i.e., diagnostic, reconstructive, curative).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the supportive care provider’s role in supporting psychological care in acute care settings (e.g., listen to the patient about their fears, refer questions about the surgery to the nurse).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the steps and procedures involved in the pre-operative and postoperative periods.

outcomes.statement: Examine how to plan, report and record patient care.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 48: Care Planning and Reporting (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 47

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the function of the care plan.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the steps in the care planning process in health care environments and in the community.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the supportive care provider’s role in the care planning process.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between objective data (i.e., information gathered based on sight, sound, smell) and subjective data (i.e., information based on patient’s report but not directly observed by others).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the criteria of an effective observation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the functions of a patient’s chart (e.g., communication, planning patient care, accountability).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the types of documents found in a patient’s chart (e.g., data forms, assessment forms, care plans, progress notes).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the types of information supportive care providers are expected to report (e.g., physical and psychological changes, nutrition, mobility, glucose-levels, report facts and not feelings).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate the use of the 24-hour clock.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain how to respect confidentiality in all aspects of a patient’s care.

outcomes.statement: Explore stress and fatigue management strategies for workers in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 49: Employee Stress and Fatigue in Health Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between eustress (i.e., healthy stress that gives a sense of fulfillment), acute stress (short in duration) and chronic stress (ongoing).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how stress can affect all dimensions of health.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the physical and emotional-behavioural signs of stress (e.g., rapid pulse, increased blood pressure, nausea, irritability, burnout, anxiety).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the signs and symptoms of burnout.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore strategies to manage stress in the workplace (e.g., develop selfawareness, take care of personal needs, think positively, ask for help, practise calming exercises).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify factors that contribute to fatigue in the work environment (e.g., personal stress, work overload, scheduling, shift work).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the effects of fatigue on role performance and injury prevention for self and patients.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe strategies for preventing fatigue.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate strategies to achieve work-life balance as a supportive care provider.

outcomes.statement: Explore the contemporary meaning and historical origins of medical terminology.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 50: Medical Terminology (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify word parts such as prefixes, roots, suffixes.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize the meanings of common Greek and Latin prefixes, roots and suffixes on which many medical terms are based.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Combine word elements to form medical terms (e.g., dys-difficult and pneabreathing become dyspnea, meaning difficulty in breathing)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate programs or courses that offer instruction on medical terminology in the local community.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Interpret medical reference points including anatomical body planes, anatomical directional terms, body cavities and abdominal regions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify and define some common abbreviation used in health care (e.g., BM – bowel movement, Dx – diagnosis, FBS - fasting blood sugar).

outcomes.statement: Examine factors related to dementia in adult patients.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 53: Dementia (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 52

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between forgetfulness and dementia.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Distinguish between disorientation, delirium and dementia.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify symptoms that could mimic those of dementia (e.g., dehydration, urinary tract infection, mood changes).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare normal and abnormal mental changes related to aging.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the signs and symptoms of dementia (e.g., forgetting names, misplacing items, becoming lost in familiar settings).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the different forms, causes and stages of dementia.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe how to support a patient living with dementia (e.g., participate in introductions at every visit, talk about plans for the day, frequently remind the patient of their location).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine why depression is often associated with dementia.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the emotional requirements of the patient diagnosed with dementia.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the role of the family in the care of the patient diagnosed with dementia.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research the impact of caring for family members with dementia on primary caregivers.

outcomes.statement: Investigate ways to support mental health of adults in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 54: Mental Health in Health Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research one or more mental health disorders such as acquired brain injuries, anxiety, depressive disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorders, schizophrenia spectrum disorders and trauma and stressor-related disorders.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine causes, signs and symptoms of depression.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss care strategies to support patients with depression.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how to support patients with mental health disorders.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify factors that may contribute to mental health disorders (e.g., biological factors, childhood experiences, stressful life events, diet).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the effects of mental health disorders on families (e.g., guilt, blame, finances).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate local adult community mental health services.

outcomes.statement: Recognize the importance of exercise and activity for patients on bed rest.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 55: Exercise and Activity for Patients on Bed Rest (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe reasons why patients may require bed rest.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate among different types of bed rest (e.g., strict bed rest, bed rest with commode privileges, bed rest with bathroom privileges).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the complications of bed rest (e.g., contracture, muscle atrophy, hypotension) and how to prevent them (e.g., moving the patient every two hours).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize the devices (e.g., bed boards, foot boards, trochanter rolls, splints, trapeze) used to support and maintain body alignment.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate a personal range of motion exercises (e.g., abduction, adduction, extension, flexion, hyperextension, rotation).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore range of motion activities that could be offered in long-term care facilities for full-time wheelchair users.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the social and emotional benefits of exercise and activity for patients on bed rest.

outcomes.statement: Investigate infection prevention strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 58: Infection Prevention (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the signs and symptoms of infection (e.g., fever and chills, nausea, rash).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine ways in which microbes are transmitted (e.g., the chain of infection) and steps to limit transmission.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss risk factors for infection (e.g., stress, poor nutrition, lack of sleep).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify routine immunizations for infection prevention.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper handwashing, cleaning and disinfection techniques.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate donning and doffing of personal protective equipment (e.g., masks, gloves, gowns).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the risks to supportive care providers and patients when infection control is not adhered to (e.g., spread of disease to a more compromised population).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research disease outbreaks including pandemic and epidemic diseases that have had significant effects on the general population past and present.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the role and responsibilities supportive care providers in preventing the spread of infection.

outcomes.statement: Examine safety measures and procedures in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 59: Safety Measures and Procedures in Health Care (Core for Supportive Care Focus) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List the risk factors for incidents (e.g., distracted or fatigued caregivers, medication, age, patients with vision, hearing or mobility challenges).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how the proper use of specialized equipment (e.g., call bells, bed rails, hand rails) can promote patient safety.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the safety measures to prevent falls, poisoning, suffocation and burns in older adults.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate health care codes that support safety (e.g., code red, blue, burgundy, white).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe guidelines to follow for emergency preparedness (e.g., in case of fire, weather event, lock down) in a health care environment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe safety guidelines to follow when using electrical equipment such as hair dryers, curling irons and electric razors with patients in health care environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain household management safety, including guidelines for dealing with pest infestations, linen and light housekeeping.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the protocol to dispose of contaminated items or waste, including sharp objects.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe measures to ensure personal safety when at work in a health care environment (e.g., when entering a patient’s home, choice of clothing and jewelry).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore the risks associated with working alone with a patient and how they can be mitigated.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the steps to reporting a workplace injury.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Explain how various emotions and reactions may block effective responses.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate grooming and dressing strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 61: Grooming and Dressing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the importance of hair care and shaving.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the factors that affect hair care.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize conditions that may be related to a patient’s hair care plan such as alopecia, dandruff and pediculosis.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how to care for matted and tangled hair.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how to provide culturally sensitive grooming.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe how to shampoo hair.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: List the steps to shave a patient.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify safety considerations related to basic nail care.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research training opportunities to learn about appropriate nail and foot care procedures.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Experiment with applying makeup or styling hair on another person according to their wishes.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe how to dress and undress patients, including patients with intravenous tubing.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Identify proper care of wigs (e.g., storage, washing, drying).

outcomes.statement: Explain ways to promote patient comfort and sleep.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 62: Patient Comfort (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize that comfort is personal to each person and based on past experiences.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify elements in a room that promote patient well-being (e.g., temperature, ventilation, odors, noise, lighting, feelings of safety).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe why comfort and well-being are important.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain why rest and sleep are important.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify factors that affect sleep (e.g., illness, nutrition, exercise, medications).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss ways to address social and emotional needs of patients winding down to sleep (e.g., spending time, talking with patients).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Suggest care plan measures that promote sleep (e.g., comfortable room temperature, clean linens, darkened room, bed positioning).

outcomes.statement: Examine common chronic conditions.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 63: Chronic Conditions (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe common chronic illnesses.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Categorize chronic conditions according to body systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between chronic pain and chronic conditions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare acute pain and chronic pain.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the effects of chronic pain on quality of life.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the concept of compassionate caring for a patient with a chronic condition and pain.

outcomes.statement: Explore nutrition, fluids and intravenous therapy in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 64A: Nutrition in Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the principles of Canada’s Food Guide, including Canada’s Dietary Guidelines.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the structure and purpose of food labels.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how nutrient requirements change throughout the life cycle.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify adult fluid requirements.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify factors that affect food choice and nutrition (e.g., personal choice, culinary culture, allergies, finances).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the social, emotional and cultural importance of meals and meal planning.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research local meal delivery services such as Meal on Wheels.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain why food safety is important (e.g., food storage, preparation and serving practices).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe special diets (e.g., sodium-controlled diets, diabetic diets, heart healthy) and why they are necessary.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the purpose of enteral nutrition (e.g., a nutritional formula delivered into the gastrointestinal tract with a tube).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of intravenous therapy (e.g., to provide needed fluids, to reverse dehydration in the body, to replace minerals and vitamins).

outcomes.statement: Examine the supportive care provider’s role in meal planning and feeding patients.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 64B: Nutrition in Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 64A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the role of the supportive care provider in meal planning and preparation (e.g., planning menus, grocery shopping, supporting special cultural dietary practices).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how to create a pleasant patient-centered dining environment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate special eating utensils available for patients with motricity issues (e.g., curved forks, special grips, plate guards).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how to feed patients, including patients who may have chewing difficulties, swallowing difficulty, vision impairments.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate feeding another person (e.g., ask them what they prefer to eat, what they would like to eat first and when they want to drink).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the supportive care provider’s role in assisting with intravenous therapy.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Plan a meal for a fictional patient with specific nutritional or cultural requirements.

outcomes.statement: Examine urinary and bowel elimination care.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 65: Elimination (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the characteristics of normal urine.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Summarize the guidelines for maintaining normal urinary elimination (e.g., provide fluids as instructed by the care plan, help the patient to the bathroom when requested).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe urinary incontinence and the care it requires (e.g., provide dry garments and linens, decrease fluid intake before bedtime, use incontinence products).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain why catheters are used.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe normal stools and the normal pattern and frequency of bowel movements.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify factors that affect bowel elimination.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the measures that promote comfort and safety during defecation.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain why enemas or suppositories are given.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Recognize how to collect urine and stool samples.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss why urine and stools specimens are collected.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe compassionate caring for the patient receiving assistance with elimination.

outcomes.statement: Explore adult hearing, vision, speech and language disorders.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 66: Adult Hearing, Vision and Speech (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the signs of hearing impairment (e.g., speaking too loudly, leaning forward to hear, responding inappropriately).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe possible effects of hearing impairment (e.g., a change in behaviour, speech challenges, frustration when communicating, increase in other senses).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine aids for patients with vision impairments (e.g., eyeglasses, contact lenses, Braille).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify communication aids and how they assist patients (e.g., communication boards, electronic devices, voice amplifier, emergency alert button).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the emotional effects of a language disorder (e.g., anger, stress, shame).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how to care for patients with speech and language disorders as an supportive care providers (e.g., be mindful of non-verbal communication, be alert for signs of fatigue, reduce surrounding distractions).

outcomes.statement: Recognize signs of abuse, bullying and harassment in a health care environment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 68: Abuse in Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the types of abuse (e.g., physical abuse, sexual abuse, emotional abuse, financial abuse, neglect).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify signs of abuse (e.g., physical injuries, a change in behaviour, unpaid bills, lack of personal hygiene).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe possible types of spousal abuse, child abuse and abuse of older persons.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how people with intellectual disabilities may be vulnerable to abuse in health care environments.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Recognize types of abuse of patients (e.g., rough handling, isolation) and health care workers (e.g., name calling, cultural slurs, physical attacks).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how to respond to abusive patient behaviour.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the supportive care provider’s responsibilities when reporting abuse in a health care environment.

outcomes.statement: Examine ways to provide end of life care.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 69: End of Life Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define palliative care.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize that personal beliefs, culture and religion influence practices and attitudes about death.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine Kübler-Ross’s five stages of grief (e.g., denial, anger, bargaining, depression and acceptance).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore how to support the emotional, social, intellectual, spiritual and physical needs of a dying patient as a supportive care provider.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify the roles and responsibilities of each member of the palliative care team.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate legal issues surrounding death and dying such as advance directives, do not resuscitate orders and medical assistance in dying.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine post-mortem care, including the possible responsibilities of the supportive care provider (e.g., may involve repositioning the body, cleaning soiled areas).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research death rituals and practices from different cultural and religious groups.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80B: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know – the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate – in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

outcomes.printedWith: Module 81B: Work Study Placement (Optional) · Suggested Time: 25-50 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 80B

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Document knowledge and awareness of employment standards, safety, workplace ethics, rights and responsibilities, occupational health and safety, and networking observed during the work placement.
