indicators.text: Integrate into performance the knowledge of standard notation conventions (e.g., note durations up to eighth notes, repeats, codas, D.S.s and dynamic markings). Identify jazz conventions that differ from traditional classical notation (e.g., falls, glisses, slides, inflection marks and hats).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Sing a variety of vocal jazz styles (e.g., swing, funk, ballad) accompanied and a cappella.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Integrate an understanding of the relationship of form and text in music, particularly blues and ABA, AABA song forms.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify different elements of music such as articulation, rhythm, beat, metre, time placement and tone that help create a jazz style and apply this knowledge while music making.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Integrate an understanding of the different elements of music such as articulation, rhythm, beat, metre, time placement and tone that help create a jazz style, and apply this knowledge while music making.

outcomes.statement: Model individual vocal techniques and apply these to create or show a musical product.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Consistently sing with a tone appropriate to the style and personal development.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Model a consistent connection between the breath and the voice.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Internalize and consistently the key concepts related to singing expressively (e.g., work painting, phrasing, motion and dynamics). Show the knowledge of these concepts through singing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Individually generate technical inquiry questions and take action on the findings of the inquiry (e.g., "What can I do to get better?" or "How could I improve this performance, paper, or arrangement?").

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Consistently use good microphone techniques in rehearsals and the performance of music.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Sing harmony a cappella maintaining key centre.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Sing a one octave chromatic scale, scending and descending, unaccompanied.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Sing one octave major, harmonic minor, dorian, mixolydian and blues scales, ascending and descending, unaccompanied.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Sing the chord tones of major and minor triads, dominant and major 7ths, major and minor 6ths and 9ths, and scale triads.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Sing a jazz standard (with recorded or live acompaniment) demonstrating scat singin and other appropriate jazz stylings.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Sight-read a simple 2 - 4 part composition

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Compare and contrast vocal jazz style to other vocal styles.

outcomes.statement: Listen and respond as a vocal jazz performer when singing jazz.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Respond to qualities of personal tone such as pitch, dynamics, style, colour, blend, rhythm, time, and consistent vowel use.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Respond to the rest of the ensemble (e.g., its tone, colour, pitch, dynamics, style, rhythm, time, balance, consistent vowel use and blend).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Immediately respond to the ensemble's response (e.g., When singing, does the student match and change vowel sounds and shapes to match the group?).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Respond to the conductor/leader, including gestures, cues, tempo, expressions and body language.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Listen to the acoustic properties of the performing space, including the sound, tone, loudness, and reverb of the room and adjust singing and microphone technique accordingly.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: React to the audience, their presence (or nor), body language, expressions and reaction to the music (e.g., applause, cheering, being asked to sing louder or quieter).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Know the history, culture, style, form and tempo of the music being performed and respond to the music by reading it and/or performing the notes and/or changes appropriately

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recall previous experiences and knowledge (in music and in life) and integrate these into solo group vocal jazz performances.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Know any special emotional context that may apply to the music, generate the appropriate emotional feeling or energy and/or synchronize the personal emotional state of the performer with the emotional context of the music being performed.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Know, predict and/or anticipate what is next or might bve next in the music and prepare for that while performing in the moment of the music.

outcomes.statement: Listen to jazz as a jazz performer when not personally performing the music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Listen to jazz music and independently analyze form, tone, style, era, dynamics, articulation, time signature, characteristic rhythms, time, balance, blend, key, monde and/or pitch.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Analyze the development of the jazz music(melody, arrangement, changes, or improvisation) as a whole or in smaller sections.
;

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the characteristic sounds, licks, tone and other elements of well-known singers and/or groups. Identify these singers and/or groups. Identify these singers and/or groups on recordings aurally, only by listening to the characteristic sounds or ideas presented in the music.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze and reflect on just one voice or instrument from the beginning to the end of a musical selection (e.g., Does the singer or player perform the same way all the way through? How was it different or the same? What did he/she sing or play that the student also might be able to sing or play?)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Listen to music analyzing and reflecting on the melody, other voices, bass line, drums and percussion, background lines, background vocals, roots and chord progression and sing with the recording.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the history, cultural heritage and effect of current events as these apply to the musical selection.

outcomes.statement: Independently analyze vocal jazz music in real time while making or listening to the music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Individually identify, experiment with, and purposefully use strategies to solve different challenges related to music making.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine common chord structures including, but not limited to, triads, seventh and ninth chords in music performed and/or listened to.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the time signatures on first hearing a piece of music, including 6/8, in addition to simpler duple time signatures. Demonstrate the patters of strong and weak beats that are identified with the time signatures

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use strategies to identify the types of scales being used (pentatonic, blues, major, etc.) in music performed and/or listened to.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop strategies for hearing 2 and 4 on first hearing a piece of music in an appropriate time signature.

outcomes.statement: Listen to performances of vocal jazz music and individually or with assistance develop and apply critical criteria to use in critical evaluation of one's own work and other's work.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Listen to the music of the great jazz and vocal jazz performers.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Generate criteria of excellence through listening to the music of the great performers (e.g., What is it that makes the music great? what do the great performers do that the student or student's ensemble does no do?)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Design and implement a plan for improvement (personal and ensemble) based on the criteria generated from listening to the great performers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Upon first hearing a musical selection, describe and classify the music using appropriate jazz language (e.g., style, period, compose, culture and performer).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Broaden knowledge of skills and components of listening actively, continue to develop these listening skill and recognize that listening contributes to the authenticity of performances.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize and discuss the value of original thought, technical proficiency, place, era and other concepts in the music of the great jazz performers.

outcomes.statement: Synthesize the knowledge and implementation of the skills, techniques and attitudes necessary for successful ensemble performance.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Know the role of each of the parts within the student's ensemble by demonstrating the ability to perform those specific tasks that are particular to the vocal part or instrument that the student sings or plays in the ensemble (e.g., bass part in the choir, comping for guitar and piano, walking lines for the bass, solo parts in the choir and position in a section).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Individually attend to melodic phrasing, rhythmic accuracy and articulation in perparation and performance of vocal jazz.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Sing in tune with good balance and tone and be aware of the qualities of the student's own voice (e.g., range, where the break in the student's voice is).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate leadership as a performer by offering help, ideas and guideance to other performers during rehearsals and sectionals.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate a professional attitude towards conduct, focus and communication skills in rehearsal, preparation of materials and presentation of products.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Consolidate the learned characteristics of different styles, eras, etc. to the performance of the student's music.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate significant understanding of PA systems including set up, tone and level settings for microphones, and so on.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Show respect for the personal work of self and others through appropriate critique.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Critically examine and assess the student's individual work and personal contributions to group projects/performances, with assistance as necessary.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Be accepting ofappropriate critiques from others, and work towards implementing the solutions to those critiques.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate and record technical development, and from that, develop strategies to improve.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Know the value of individual practice, know how to practive, conduct an ongoing evaluation of the student's personal practice skills, and implement a plan for improvement.

outcomes.statement: Aurally distinguish the different eras, genres, styles and feels of vocal jazz through listening to and/or performing the representative music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Individually listen to recording of vocal jazz, develop a list or understanding of the basic characteristics of different jazz styles, genres, periods and place and implement that knowledge into practice and performance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: On first hearing, catagorize jazz music into styles, genres, periods and/or place.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine aspects of jazz such as history, performers, styles and eras through a variety of media, with a focus on Canadian or Saskatchewan jazz artists.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate awareness of vocal jazz music by suggesting listening and/or performing opportunities for the ensemble.

outcomes.statement: Explore jazz music and its performers and educators and their influence in the world.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine roles that vocal jazz artists might have beyond being performers, and identify individuals who fit those particular roles (e.g., Bobby McFerrin, Phil Mattson, and Gene Puerling).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: A number of jazz artists have First Nations or American Indian heritage (e.g., Mildred Bailey, Lena Horne, Joe Williams and Julia Keefe). Discuss possible reasons why this is not widley known and the effect that this heritage may have had on their music and lives.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify influential singers or players of the student's instrument, investigate why these performers are so influential and listen to their music. Give special attention to performers from Saskatchewan and Canada.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the influence of jazz on contemporary First Nations music.

outcomes.statement: Evaluate the degree of influence that vocal jazz has had on other types of music with an emphasis on the music of Canada and Saskatchewan, and assess possible careers in vocal jazz and music

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the influence of jazz in pop, rock and other current music (e.g., the use of jazz themes and rhythms in hip-hop, rap, funk), and the influence of these current styles on jazz.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the relationship between instrumental and vocal jazz, with particular emphasis on on vocalese.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe how Canadian and international copyright laws affect the lives of those who work in the jazz field.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research career pathways in vocal jazz and music in general.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine "crossover" artists and how categorization of music affects the artist and musical product.

outcomes.statement: Examine the methods and reasons for monitoring wildlife populations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17: Wildlife Populations (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the cultural and traditional stories and knowledge about the relationship between animals and Indigenous people with an Elder or Knowledge Keeper.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Discuss the reasons for studying wildlife populations, including:
- understanding the impact of environmental change;
- game management; and,
- monitoring threatened species.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare various scientific methods (e.g., quadrat study, interpolation, stem count and estimating) used to count populations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Conduct a population study using an appropriate method, such as:
- scat analysis (e.g., deer and rabbit density);
- pond dipping; and,
- fish trapping or seine netting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Use a variety of resources (e.g., Knowledge Keeper, books and technological applications) to identify birds in a given ecosystem.

indicators.label: f

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of completing a bird survey.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze what the results of a population study indicate about the health of the species and the environment.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate the impact that overpopulated wildlife species in Saskatchewan have on other species and the environment.

indicators.label: j

indicators.label: k

indicators.text: Investigate provincial and federal measures used to determine if a species or population is endangered.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss factors that affect wildlife populations within selected ecoregions of Saskatchewan and Canada, such as habitat loss, climate change, commercial harvest and disease.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine strategies used to bring at-risk wildlife populations back to healthy levels.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the impact that industrial activity (e.g., mining, hydroelectric, forestry and agriculture) has on ecosystems and wildlife populations.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research the impact of invasive animal species (e.g., wild boars) and aquatic species (e.g., zebra mussels) on local wildlife.

indicators.label: g
h
indicators.text: Explain the relationship between stressed wildlife habitats and zoonosis (i.e., unhealthy habitat leads to prevalence and mutation of wildlife disease).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore how wildlife can become a vector for transmission of diseases to humans (e.g., rabies, lyme disease, West Nile virus and coronavirus disease).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the significance of biodiversity in preventing disease.

indicators.label: k

indicators.text: Examine different levels of wildlife protection legislation (i.e., provincial and federal) and their connection to non-profit organizations.

indicators.label: m

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80B: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III - Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse - work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement. These may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one's performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement:
Demonstrate concretely, pictorially, and symbolically an understanding of limitations of measuring instruments including:
- precision
- accuracy
- uncertainty
- tolerance.
outcomes.printedWith: [C, PS, R, T, V]

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain, using concrete models and pictorial representations, the difference between precision and accuracy.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Analyze given contexts to generalize and explain why:
- a certain degree of precision is required
- a certain degree of accuracy is required.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare the degree of accuracy of two or more given instruments used to measure the same attribute.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Relate the degree (margin) of accuracy to the uncertainty of a given measure.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze and justify the degree of precision and accuracy required in contextual problems.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze given contexts to calculate maximum and minimum values, using a given degree (range) of tolerance.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare and describe, using examples, the limitations of measuring instruments used in a specific trade or industry, (e.g., tape measure versus Vernier caliper).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Create and solve situational questions that involve precision, accuracy, or tolerance, and explain the reasoning and the strategy used to arrive at the solution.

outcomes.statement:

indicators.label: a

indicators.text:
Draw the image of 2-D shapes given:

- a combination of successive transformations and explain the reasoning.

indicators.text: Create designs using translations, rotations, and reflections in all four quadrants of a coordinate grid.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze and describe designs that involve translations, rotations, and reflections in all four quadrants of a coordinate grid, and explain the reasoning.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research and present, orally, in writing, or using multimedia, applications of transformations using examples and illustrations in construction, industrial, commercial, domestic, and artistic contexts.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze and generalize the relationship between reflections and lines or planes of symmetry.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain how and why the concept of similarity can be used to determine if an image is a dilation of a given shape, and provide examples.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Determine whether or not given images are dilations of given shapes and explain the reasoning.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Draw, with or without technology, a dilation image for a given 2-D shape and 3-D object, and explain how the original 2-D shape or 3-D object and its image are proportional.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Solve contextual problems that involve transformations and explain the reasoning.

Employ the following German language conventions consistently in oral and written texts:
- accusative and dative adjective endings (e.g., “Sie haben eine große Mauer aus dickem Beton im 1961 in Berlin gebaut.”);
- relative pronouns and conjunctions with accurate word order (e.g., “Ich habe ein Sweatshirt am Alexanderplatz für meine Schwester gekauft, weil sie es zum Geburtstag gewünscht hat.”); and,
- modal verbs with accurate word order (e.g., “Wenn es wieder warm ist, will ich sofort draußen am See schwimmen.”).

Produce a variety of oral Spanish texts related to big ideas such as:
- global Spanish communities;
- media and technology; and,
- future plans.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Contribute to spontaneous conversations on familiar topics with multiple participants.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Generate conversations by posing and responding to questions on a variety of topics, such as travel experiences, school aspirations and entertainment preferences.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Experiment with oral language to communicate emotions, opinions and advice.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Act as a middle person in informal situations by relaying basic information from English to short, simple Spanish and vice versa.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Provide detailed directions to a location.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conduct an interview by posing, and responding to, direct questions.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Present stories, poetry and monologues with expression, intonation and enunciation.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Defend opinions with supporting arguments in a debate.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Persuade audience of a perspective using convincing details and supporting arguments.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Present information on a topic of interest (e.g., sports, music and travel destination) using a variety of visuals (e.g., charts, maps, diagrams, pictures and gestures) while speaking.

indicators.label: l

outcomes.statement: Produce a variety of written non-fiction and fiction Spanish texts to express ideas, extend knowledge of the world, achieve objectives and for enjoyment.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Produce a variety of written Spanish texts related to big ideas such as:
- global Spanish communities;
- media and technology; and,
- future plans.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Complete a questionnaire or résumé with relevant details (e.g., education, skills, work experience and interests).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Write a message to convey the details (e.g., time and location) of an appointment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compose emails requesting information on topics related to future plans (e.g., travel or exchange possibilities, post-secondary education and career opportunities).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create a comic strip with Spanish dialogue.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Express personal opinions in a persuasive text (e.g., travel blogs and editorials).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Experiment with a variety of text types (e.g., letters, schedules, lists, questionnaires, reports and social media posts).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research, organize and present information in expository texts (e.g., biography on Spanish artist and essay on traditional Spanish foods).

indicators.label: i

outcomes.statement: Explore historical and contemporary elements, and the cultural and linguistic diversity, of Spanish cultures around the world.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify Spanish-speaking countries (e.g., Spain, Argentina, Mexico and Nicaragua) in the world.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research significant historical and contemporary events (e.g., Aztec and Inca empires, independence from Spain and Portugal, construction of Panama Canal, Cuban and Mexican revolution) that affect Spanish communities.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the traditional and cultural contributions of Spanish-speakers (e.g., Pablo Picasso, Antonio Banderas, Rigoberta Menchu, Manuela Saenz and Isabel Allende).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare dialectical pronunciation and vocabulary differences within Spanish and in standard usage in other parts of the world.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the economic impact of Spain within Europe and on other countries around the world.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Inquire about Spanish culture and heritage (e.g., the arts, celebrations, community, traditions, language, history and food) in various parts of the world by:
- reading, listening to or viewing tourist information or facts about Spanish-speaking countries or regions around the world;
- researching Spanish festivals, events and organizations (e.g., La Tomatina, Día de los Muertos, San Fermin and Santiago de Cuba); and,
- investigating cultural places or historic sites (e.g., Teotihuacatan and La Sagrada Familia).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine and compare elements of Spanish culture and heritage (e.g., food, the arts, celebrations, community, traditions, language, history) in various parts of the world.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate the impact of Spanish communities’ geographical locations on their local culture and ethnic diversity.

indicators.label: i

outcomes.statement: Investigate international opportunities to use and develop Spanish language skills and explore personal identity as a Spanish language learner.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain how personal understanding of a culture might be enhanced through language learning.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify study opportunities at Spanish-speaking universities and technical colleges (e.g., National University of Mexico City, Spanish Immersion in Costa Rica and Spanish Immersion courses with Buenos Aires Institute) open to international students.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore international summer work opportunities and practicum placements for Spanishspeaking students.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the different linguistic and cultural perspectives on world issues (e.g., violence, sexuality, the environment and social media).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate opportunities to communicate in Spanish at the global level (e.g., Spanish social media groups, blogging, corresponding in Spanish with people from various parts of the Spanish-speaking world).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research global opportunities to further personal Spanish language learning (e.g., postsecondary programs, international cultural exchanges and organizations).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate international scholarship, study and travel opportunities (e.g., VolSol) available to Spanish-speaking Canadian students.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore international career fields for which the ability to speak Spanish is a requirement or an asset (e.g., the Red Cross, Olympics, United Nations, business, interpreter, international government, education, reporters and Doctors without Borders).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore worldwide programming and initiatives that support Spanish communities, programming and language.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect on personal linguistic and cultural identity.

evidence.observation: The outcomes page groups the outcomes under 12 unit headings.
